text: 8. Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Allows two parties (Alice & Bob) to agree on a shared secret key without revealing it to eavesdroppers. 1. Choose a large prime 1 and a base g. Both are public. 2. e Alice picks a secret a, computes A = g° mod n and sends A. « Bob picks a secret b, computes B = g mod n and sends B. 3. ¢ Alice computes K = B® mod n. « Bob computes K = A’ mod n. 4. Both get the same shared key K. Example: Ifn =23,g=5,a=4,b=3: « Alice sends A = 5% mod 23 = 625 mod 23 = 8. « Bobsends B =5 mod 23 = 125 mod 23 = 10. « Both compute K = 10* mod 23 = 8% mod 23 = 2 (whichever expression you use, you get 2).
